summary: Specifies packetization for 12-bit nonlinear, 20-bit linear, and 24-bit linear audio in RTP, and defines an SDP parameter indicating preemphasis.

eli5.summary: It describes how to pack high-quality sound into packages for sending live.

questions: what is the sdp emphasis parameter
how are multichannel audio samples ordered in rtp
subtitle: How to carry 12-bit, 20-bit and 24-bit digital audio in RTP packets, plus a way to flag preemphasis.

tldr.problem: Digital audio tape and digital video devices use 12-bit nonlinear, 20-bit linear and 24-bit linear samples, but only 16-bit linear audio (L16) had an RTP payload format.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3190 defines how to pack those samples contiguously into RTP payloads, names the formats DAT12, L20 and L24, and adds two SDP and MIME parameters: emphasis for preemphasized audio and channel-order for multichannel streams.
tldr.outcome: Senders can transmit these audio formats without converting them to 16 bits, and the emphasis parameter can also be used with L16. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no replacement.

today: RFC 3190 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 1890 and the L16 format, and its companion for DV video is RFC 3189.

sections.title: Why New Audio Payload Formats
sections.content:
High-quality digital audio and video systems such as DAT (digital audio tape) and DV (digital video) use sample-based audio encodings. To send such audio with the Real-time Transport Protocol, each format needs its own encapsulation. At the time of this RFC only 16-bit linear audio (L16) had one.

DAT and DV devices also use 12-bit nonlinear, 20-bit linear and 24-bit linear encodings. RFC 3190 follows the L16 packetization scheme for these, so the encoding-independent rules for sample ordering and channel interleaving from the RTP profile still apply, with extensions specified here.
sections.eli5: Some fancy recorders store sound in bigger or smaller chunks than the usual size. This RFC says how to put those odd chunk sizes into network parcels.

sections.title: Packing 12-bit, 20-bit and 24-bit Samples
sections.content:
The 12-bit nonlinear format is the LP (Long Play) audio of IEC 61119. Each sample comes from a 16-bit linear sample through a nonlinear compression given in a table in the RFC. The result is a signed value from -2048 to 2047 in two's complement. Converting to 16-bit linear and using L16 would work, but would use 33% more bandwidth than necessary.

The 20-bit and 24-bit linear formats are plain extensions of L16: uncompressed signed samples in two's complement. In all three formats the samples are packed contiguously, most significant bit first, with the oldest sample first. When a 12-bit or 20-bit payload holds an odd number of samples, the four least significant bits of the last octet are unused. Sampling frequency and channel assignment work as in L16.

In SDP the encoding names are DAT12, L20 and L24, for example a=rtpmap:97 DAT12/32000/2.
sections.eli5: Samples are like beads of a fixed size laid end to end in a tube. The 12-bit and 20-bit sizes can leave a half-bead gap at the end, which is just left empty.

sections.title: Preemphasis Parameter
sections.content:
Analog preemphasis is often applied before quantization to improve the higher frequency characteristics of a signal. If it was applied before sampling, the sender SHOULD say so out of band with an emphasis parameter, as a MIME optional parameter or in an SDP line like a=fmtp:<payload type> emphasis=<emphasis type>.

Only one value is defined: 50-15, meaning 50/15 microsecond CD-type emphasis. The attribute MUST NOT appear if preemphasis was not applied. That keeps it backward compatible, including with L16. A receiver that ignores it only produces sound that is too bright when receiving or too dull when sending.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the treble is boosted before recording. This note tells the listener, so they can turn it back down and the sound comes out right.

sections.title: DV Audio Error Codes
sections.content:
The DV specification reserves the negative full-scale sample value as an error code that means no valid sample is available, for example after a tape read failure. The values are 800h for 12-bit nonlinear, 8000h for 16-bit linear and 80000h for 20-bit linear. In the RTP formats no such code exists and every value is a valid sample.

A sender taking audio from a DV system SHOULD run some error concealment, which the RFC leaves to the implementation. It MAY pass the error code through as a valid sample, but that is likely to sound bad. A receiver delivering audio to a DV system SHOULD translate samples that would read as error codes to the next smaller negative value. For 20-bit audio, the values 80000h to 8000Fh all become 80010h. No translation is given for 24-bit audio, since DV does not include it.
sections.eli5: On the tape, one special value means "this bit is broken". On the network that value is just a sound, so the sender should patch the hole and the receiver should avoid accidentally showing the broken marker.

sections.title: Channel Interleaving and Channel Order
sections.content:
With several channels in one RTP stream, samples are interleaved as in L16. Samples from different channels taken at the same sampling instant are packed into consecutive octets, and all samples for one instant MUST be in the same packet. For two channels the order is left first sample, right first sample, left second sample, right second sample.

This differs from native DV audio blocks, so applications sending DV audio in these formats MUST reshuffle samples. Streams of 1, 2 or 3 channels use the implicit AIFF-C order, and for those the channel-order parameter MUST NOT be included. For DV streams of 4 or more channels, the order MUST be given out of band as channel-order=<convention>.<order>. The only convention defined is DV, with orders such as LRLsRs for 4 channels or LRLsRsC for 5. The parameter MUST agree with the channel count.

The RFC advises that if audio can be sent in AIFF-C order after simple shuffling, the AIFF-C order SHOULD be used, for interoperability. Independent audio channels, such as translations in several languages, SHOULD go in separate RTP sessions so receivers can pick only what they want.
sections.eli5: When there is a left and a right speaker, their sounds take turns in the parcel: left, right, left, right. For bigger setups the extra note says exactly who goes in which seat.

sections.title: MIME Registrations and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC registers three MIME subtypes under audio: DAT12, L20 and L24. Each has a required rate parameter, with recommended values 8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100 and 48000 samples per second, and optional channels, emphasis and channel-order parameters. The channels default is 1.

The registrations differ in which DV channel orders apply. For DAT12 all permissible orders except DV.LmixRmixTWoQ1Q2 are used with DV systems, while for L20 only mono and stereo are allowed with DV. The IANA section says that anyone wanting new values for emphasis or channel-order must produce a revision of the document through the normal standards process.
sections.eli5: The names of the new formats go into an official list so everyone spells them the same way, and nobody can add new options without going through a proper process.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Packets in these formats are subject to the security considerations of the RTP specification and of the RTP profile. Confidentiality is achieved by encrypting the media stream. The RFC notes that any compression used is applied end to end, so encryption may be done after compression.

It also discusses denial of service. Encodings with non-uniform decoding cost could let an attacker inject datagrams that are costly to decode, but this encoding does not show significant non-uniformity. As with any IP protocol, a receiver may also be overloaded by too many packets.
sections.eli5: To keep the sound private, lock the parcel. The packing here is simple, so nobody can slow the listener down by sending parcels that are very hard to open.

viz.caption: SDP EXAMPLE FROM THE RFC: PREEMPHASIS ON ONE PAYLOAD TYPE

data.title: Preemphasis in SDP
data.code:
m=audio 49230 RTP/AVP 99 100
a=rtpmap:99 L20/48000/2
a=fmtp:99 emphasis=50-15
a=rtpmap:100 L24/48000
